They also call include_permno, ffsic, leadlag_qtr and WT; those external macro definitions are not supplied. issues.description: The target is the supplied two-program SAS workflow. The source-visible local WORK.SAMPLE to remote TMP.FIRMS upload to WORK.FIRMS consumer chain is identified, but remote session availability, SAMPLE1/SAMPLE2 source fields and history, required macros, and many other author-prepared or raw inputs lack confirmed producer-to-consumer closure. The identifiers file is not an analysis dataset. No analysis-only bypass is supported by the supplied materials.

Both programs include two external SAS macro files. Active calls include include_permno, ffsic, leadlag_qtr and WT; their definitions, inputs and outputs are not supplied. The local %test123 definition is visible, but its PROC TTEST capability still needs SAS/STAT support.

The first program constructs local WORK.SAMPLE from SAMPLE1 and SAMPLE2, begins a remote-submit block, names libref identifiers, uploads SAMPLE as TMP.FIRMS, and later copies/filters TMP.FIRMS into WORK.FIRMS. The original pre-read scan flagged candidate connection/authentication lines 89-90; those values and all libref RHS/path values remain withheld. Actual session/connection availability, software support, SAMPLE1/SAMPLE2 field/history contracts, and remote source data are unverified. Do not expose or copy credentials into the assessment.

The package contains only the identifier dataset alongside code and the datasheet. Multiple consumed call, analyst, label, mapping and control inputs are absent, and bounded catalog hits do not verify the required complete history or author-specific field contracts. The requested raw and author-prepared inputs are alternatives where they provide the same authored input; they are not jointly required duplicates.

The supplied programs use SAS procedures including SQL, SORT, MEANS, FREQ, PRINT, RANK, TTEST, EXPORT and remote PROC DOWNLOAD within a remote-submit block, plus custom macros. The environment record reports SAS startup failure at TKELS; SAS/STAT support for PROC TTEST, SAS/CONNECT support for the remote steps, and the DBMS=STATA export engine are unverified. No SAS/ETS use was identified, and the environment failure is not evidence of an absent license.

The main program reads the existing total_analysts member before replacing it. The supplemental section also repeatedly writes perm.FGLS after reading it. Preserve the initial input members and each required intermediate in a working-copy archive before any future run.

steps: Obtain the exact author macro files or written macro definitions for include_permno, ffsic, leadlag_qtr and WT; document each macro's input fields, output members and required history.

Preserve the visible order: combine SAMPLE1 and SAMPLE2 into local WORK.SAMPLE, enter the remote-submit block, upload SAMPLE as TMP.FIRMS, then copy/filter TMP.FIRMS into WORK.FIRMS. review_notes: Assessment is limited to the supplied variant: two SAS source programs, one datasheet/appendix and an identifier dataset. The identifier file is not a usable analysis input; no analysis_only scope is supported.

The work-item source hashes and package archive hashes remain the frozen provenance. Source evidence quotes are exact, one-based slices from the assigned cached content; the first program's candidate connection/authentication block was conservatively withheld at lines 65-110 after a static scan flagged lines 89-90.

No author code, SAS runtime, model, regression or data-construction program was executed. The SAS startup failure and bounded catalog/probe results are not license or full-coverage evidence. Each successful SAS data probe reads at most one row; no whole-file counts or population coverage are inferred.

A prior initial field request failed because the selected COMP.FUNDQ/KLD fields were absent. Those requests, errors and original probes remain preserved. Corrected one-row probes used only fields present in the candidates; COMP.FUNDQ still lacks SIC/INSTOWN in the selected fields and KLD.HISTORY lacks the required ticker join.

The source directly reads IBES EXCU, RECDDET and ACTU tables in addition to the prepared call, analyst and control inputs. These direct inputs were retained even when not represented as standalone checklist edges.

The supplied programs contain active PROC SQL, SORT, MEANS, FREQ, PRINT, RANK, TTEST and EXPORT calls. SAS/STAT and DBMS=STATA export support remain unverified. External macros include include_permno, ffsic, leadlag_qtr and WT; the test123 macro is defined in program 1. No SAS/ETS use was identified.

Program 0 opens a block comment at line 473 that remains open through EOF; the tail is inactive in the supplied file. Program 1 reads total_analysts before rewriting that member and repeatedly writes perm.FGLS in its supplemental section; a working-copy archive is required.

The appendix reports analyses, but the two supplied programs contain no standalone regression-stage program. A separate Stata regression stage is not added without a real operational source/call. No new ethnicity, race, religion, nationality or other protected-trait inference was performed from names, photos, people or companies; author-prepared label inputs were assessed only as declared fields.

The datasheet describes Factiva transcript use, LinkedIn photos for the authors' verification process and Compustat/CRSP/IBES data. Those descriptions do not close the missing file/schema/history contracts; contact details and personal identifiers are not copied into the assessment.
A separate process_trace.json records retained catalog/probe and helper capture metadata. It is custody/process history only and is not cited recursively as scientific evidence.
